problem_summary.summary: Implement a fixed-capacity least-recently-used cache whose get and put operations refresh recency and whose insertion evicts the least recently used key when full.
problem_summary.input_output: Implement LRUCache(int capacity), int get(int key), and void put(int key, int value). No external node type is used; the implementation defines private doubly linked nodes. Capacity is positive.

brute_force.explanation: Keep entries in a doubly linked list ordered from most to least recent. Use a linear search for keys; after a hit or update, move that entry to the front, and evict the tail when capacity is exceeded.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The list order explicitly tracks recency, so moving every used entry to the front and removing the tail implements LRU exactly. Linear search makes this a clear baseline but not the required average O(1) design.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(capacity) per get or put due to linear key search.

optimized.explanation: Combine a HashMap from keys to entries with a doubly linked recency list. The front is most recent; the back is least recent. Hash lookup and constant-time list relinking support O(1) average operations.
optimized.correctness_idea: The map identifies an entry directly, while the linked list maintains exact recency order. Every successful get or put moves its entry to the front; inserting beyond capacity removes the back neighbor, which is the least recently used entry.
optimized.time_complexity: O(1) average per get and put, assuming expected O(1) HashMap operations.
optimized.space_complexity: O(capacity) for the map and recency list.
